title: Dissector-side defects in consumers of Wireshark's wmem pools: fourteen temporal, nine spatial
note: Cases 0-12 and 22 are temporal; cases 13-21 are SPATIAL, from the hunt recorded in docs/ref/wireshark-spatial-defect-triage.md. Cases 14 and 15 are the corpus's only rows LIVE at the v4.6.8 pin -- every other row, temporal and spatial alike, is a fix-reversal. Note for anyone reading the spatial rows: every arm of this harness narrows a wmem allocation to its request (wm_narrow(), ports/wireshark/wmem/src/shared/wmem-port-hooks.h:11-15), so a spatial crossing faults on ALL arms and these rows do not discriminate the chunk port. Case 13's run established that by refuting its own prediction. Cases 18-21 added 2026-10-07, all SPATIAL and all nested. 18 (716a200295) is the row that FILLS a cell this inventory recorded as empty: a nested-spatial defect LIVE at the v4.6.8 pin, whose guard cannot fire because the user preference it tests defaults to 0. The leads came from bug-corpora/wireshark/LIVE-CANDIDATES.md and from the class-B candidates docs/ref/wireshark-spatial-defect-triage.md:226-229 named and left unbuilt. Two candidates from those lists were REJECTED rather than built: 1c090e9292 is a STACK buffer overflow, so it has no heap allocator boundary, and d7d1686a95 indexes a static value_string array, which likewise has no allocator. 0939cf989d is the same ETSI DCP defect as case 16 under a different hash. Case 22 added 2026-10-11 from the nested-shape hunt (docs/ref/nested-shape-hunt-2026-10.md): c702b44a01, a fix reversal, the corpus's first double free (S2) -- two USB HID OUTPUT fields share one usages array and the error path frees it twice into the file scope's BLOCK allocator, corrupting its in-band recycler list (S4). Its defective access is a call into the allocator, so its protected oracles name the allocator's handback (wm_widen_probe, wm_widen), declared in its fault_sites before any protected run.
